overview: The Docker Cleanup Playbook is a battle-tested shell script designed for developers drowning in unpruned volumes, dangling images, and stopped containers that eat up SSD space. It inspects your local Docker environment and generates a precise, customized cleanup script without executing anything blindly. It helps busy software engineers reclaim gigabytes of disk space safely and transparently, without the anxiety of accidentally wiping a database container they actually need.
usecases: Freeing up hundreds of gigabytes of disk space on a developer laptop when Docker suddenly warns you that storage is critically low.
Cleaning up abandoned test environments and dangling build cache layers generated by CI pipelines or local testing.
Auditing what Docker actually plans to delete before running a destructive command on a shared development server.
howto: Download the standalone script file to your local machine.
Grant execution permissions using chmod +x docker-cleanup.sh.
Run the script in your terminal to inspect the generated cleanup plan and copy the commands you want.

faq.q: Will this script automatically delete my running containers or active volumes?
faq.a: No, the playbook operates in dry-run mode by default and only outputs suggested commands for your review.

faq.q: Why use a script instead of just running docker system prune -a?
faq.a: Generic prune commands are notoriously blunt instruments that often wipe out cache layers and volumes you actually wanted to keep.
